body:
PENNSYLVANIA DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH Policy Number: 5.01 WIC State Agency USDA Approval Date: February 20, 2024 State Effective Date: April 20, 2024

POLICY MANUAL 5. WIC NUTRITION AND BREASTFEEDING SERVICES. 5.01 Nutrition Education and Counseling.

Page 1 of 6

A. POLICY OVERVIEW PA WIC shall make nutrition education available to all participants at no cost to promote healthy food and lifestyle choices.

B. POLICY 1. Planning Nutrition Contacts:

a. Nutrition education and counseling shall be made available to adult participants, parents or caregivers of infant and child participants, and whenever possible, child participants themselves.

b. Each participant shall be offered a minimum of four nutrition education contacts during each one-year certification period. For participants certified less than one year, nutrition education must be offered at the equivalent of one contact for every three months. The contacts shall be made available at four separate clinic visits, on four different dates.

c. The local agency (LA) shall have a procedure to reschedule participants who miss appointments that include nutrition education. The procedure shall assure that appropriate staff is available to provide nutrition education at the rescheduled appointment.

d. Routine nutrition education contacts may be provided by Certified Professional Authorities (CPAs), Competent Paraprofessional Authorities (CPPAs) and Program Assistants, designated by the LA. High-risk nutrition education contacts shall be provided in accordance with the guidelines listed in Section 4, Provision of Nutrition Education and Counseling for High-Risk Participants.

e. If the parent or caregiver is not present at the WIC appointment, nutrition education shall be made available to a proxy of a participant and the proxy shall be encouraged to share the information with the party represented.

f. The LA shall not require nutrition education as a condition to participate in the WIC program and may not withhold benefits when nutrition education is declined but shall document any failure or inability to participate in the Management Information System (MIS) for purposes of future nutrition education efforts and program monitoring.

PENNSYLVANIA DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH Policy Number: 5.01 WIC State Agency USDA Approval Date: February 20, 2024 State Effective Date: April 20, 2024

POLICY MANUAL 5. WIC NUTRITION AND BREASTFEEDING SERVICES. 5.01 Nutrition Education and Counseling.

Page 2 of 6

2. Provision of Nutrition Education and Counseling:

a. The purpose of nutrition education and counseling is to emphasize the relationship between nutrition, physical activity and health outcomes, and to assist participants in making positive changes in dietary and physical activity behaviors.

b. Nutrition education and counseling may occur in person or in accordance with the most current teleWIC guidance issued by the State agency (SA).

c. Nutrition education shall be made available through individual or group sessions covering topics that are appropriate to individual participant’s needs with consideration of the following:

(1) Nutritional needs and concerns as determined via Nutrition Assessment. (2) Food preferences. (3) Level of motivation and barriers to making positive changes. (4) Educational abilities and preferred learning styles. (5) Environmental influences/household situation. (6) Geographic location. (7) Cultural, ethnic, socioeconomic factors, and language needs. d. Nutrition education shall include a conversation with the participant. The following methods may be used to supplement, but may not replace, individual or group nutrition education:

(1) Pamphlets or newsletters (provided in-person, electronically, or by mail). (2) Posters, bulletin boards, or displays. (3) Information from reliable websites such as WIC-Works Resource Center, Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, Fruits and Veggies More Matters, Nemours KidsHealth.org, etc. (4) Audiovisual aids. (5) Educational props, such as food models, puzzles, games, etc. (6) Online nutrition education lessons. (7) Text messaging. (8) Education provided by partner organizations, unless approved by the SA.

e. Nutrition education for participants should include the following six elements:

(1) Consideration of participant risks, needs and concerns. (2) Setting individual, simple and attainable goals and providing ways to accomplish the goals. (3) Counseling methods that are easily understood.

PENNSYLVANIA DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH Policy Number: 5.01 WIC State Agency USDA Approval Date: February 20, 2024 State Effective Date: April 20, 2024

POLICY MANUAL 5. WIC NUTRITION AND BREASTFEEDING SERVICES. 5.01 Nutrition Education and Counseling.

Page 3 of 6

(4) Opportunities for interaction and feedback. (5) Reinforcements: pamphlets, bulletin boards, toothbrushes, cups, etc. (6) Follow-up to assess for behavior change.

f. Nutrition education should be based on a Value Enhanced Nutrition Assessment (VENA). In accordance with the USDA’s VENA initiative, the nutrition assessment shall include data collection and the application of critical thinking across the assessment categories. g. Goal setting is an important component of VENA and, therefore, required at initial certifications, re-certifications, and health evaluations. The following are considered acceptable reasons goal setting may not occur at initial certifications, re-certifications, and health evaluations: i) The participant declines setting a goal after staff have made a good faith effort to engage them in the guided goal setting process. ii) A need that takes priority over other risks (e.g. unstable housing, unsafe or inadequate childcare, domestic abuse concerns) has been identified during the nutrition assessment.

h. Goal setting is considered a best practice at benefit pick-up appointments and is strongly encouraged for all participants who are high-risk.

i. Exit counseling, including State-provided exit counseling brochure, shall be offered to all women “graduating” from the WIC program during the final appointment within both the pregnancy and postpartum certification periods.

(1) Exit counseling shall emphasize a well-balanced diet, folic acid intake, breastfeeding promotion, importance of children’s immunizations and the health risks of alcohol, smoking and using drugs. (2) Exit counseling sessions may be waived to provide risk-specific nutrition counseling when deemed more appropriate, but the exit counseling brochure must still be provided. The reason for waiving the exit counseling session must be clearly documented in the MIS. (3) All exit counseling sessions and the provision of exit counseling brochures must be documented in the MIS. j. LA staff must educate on lead poisoning prevention, immunization screening schedule, and substance use/abuse as determined necessary during the nutrition assessment. Refer to Policy 5.00, Nutrition and Risk Assessment, for details on when screenings, provision of information related to these topics and referrals must be provided.

k. All nutrition education provided must be consistent with information from nationally recognized sources, such as the American College of Obstetrics and Gynecology, American Academy of Pediatrics, Bright Futures, USDA WIC Infant Feeding Guide,

PENNSYLVANIA DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH Policy Number: 5.01 WIC State Agency USDA Approval Date: February 20, 2024 State Effective Date: April 20, 2024

POLICY MANUAL 5. WIC NUTRITION AND BREASTFEEDING SERVICES. 5.01 Nutrition Education and Counseling.

Page 4 of 6

MyPlate, More Matters, FNS Core Nutrition Messages, and Dietary Guidelines for Americans. USDA guidance shall be deferred to when recommendations differ between other reputable sources.

3. Documentation of Nutrition Education and Counseling:

a. Nutrition education and counseling shall be documented in the MIS for each participant by both selecting nutrition education topic code(s) and recording specific education and counseling that took place during the appointment.

(1) Nutrition education topics should be selected only if there was substantial discussion on the topic, including provision of specific suggestions. Topics should not be selected if the topic was simply mentioned during the course of routine assessment. b. Documentation for nutrition education contacts at initial certifications, re-certifications, and health evaluations must include goal follow-up (if applicable), complete nutrition assessment, interpretation of weight gain/growth, justification/interpretation of assigned risk codes, nutrition education topics, nutrition education/counseling description, and a goal.

c. Documentation for nutrition education contacts at appointment types other than initial certifications, re-certifications, and health evaluations must include goal follow-up (if applicable), nutrition assessment update (changes since last assessment), nutrition education topics, referrals, nutrition education/counseling description, and a goal (if applicable).

4. Provision of Nutrition Education and Counseling for High-Risk Participants:

a. High-risk nutrition services are intended for participants who are at higher risk for nutrition or health problems that can be prevented or improved through appropriate nutrition intervention.

b. WIC staff shall identify participants who are at high-risk and require special nutrition intervention. Participants may be identified as high-risk at any time during a certification period. High-risk status must be indicated in the MIS. Where applicable, physical charts for high-risk participants should be readily identifiable using a marker, color coded folder or other system.

c. High-risk nutrition care should be individualized, timely, and directed at stabilizing or improving the risk condition(s). Services required are the same as non-high-risk participants but must be provided, monitored and documented by a CPA. CPAs have

PENNSYLVANIA DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH Policy Number: 5.01 WIC State Agency USDA Approval Date: February 20, 2024 State Effective Date: April 20, 2024

POLICY MANUAL 5. WIC NUTRITION AND BREASTFEEDING SERVICES. 5.01 Nutrition Education and Counseling.

Page 5 of 6

the discretion to determine whether more frequent nutrition care is needed for a high- risk participant.

d. When a CPA is not available, a CPPA may provide and document the high-risk care. When a CPPA provides services to a high-risk participant, a CPA must review and approve the documented contact. When additional follow up is deemed necessary by a CPA, a high-risk follow up with a CPA must take place within 10 business days of the appointment with the CPPA. CPA approval of high-risk care provided by the CPPA and/or any additional follow up needed must be documented in the MIS.

e. For participants who are high-risk for the reason of receiving Food Package III, refer to Policy 5.10, Exempt Infant Formulas and WIC-Eligible Nutritionals, regarding food package prescription requirements.

f. High-risk contacts shall be documented in the MIS according to State agency guidance.

g. High-risk status can be discontinued by a CPA, except for participants receiving exempt infant formulas or WIC-eligible nutritionals, when the problem(s) no longer exist(s), the condition is stable, or the participant leaves the WIC Program. (1) If a participant is determined to no longer be high-risk, CPAs must document in the MIS that high-risk status has been resolved and include the justification. (2) CPAs may determine that it is beneficial to continue high-risk status after the condition is stable to prevent regression.

h. The LA Nutrition Education Coordinator shall train staff on high-risk nutrition services in accordance with Policy 3.03, Training of WIC Staff.

5. Nutrition Education Plans:

a. The LA shall develop and submit to the SA an annual nutrition education plan in accordance with the guidance distributed by the SA.

b. Annual nutrition education plans shall be prepared by the Nutrition Education Coordinator using the written guidance provided by the SA. When feasible, all staff that provides nutrition education should be given the opportunity to participate in developing the LA’s nutrition education plan.

c. All staff that provides nutrition education at the LA shall be familiar with Federal and SA requirements for nutrition education and shall be familiar with the LA’s nutrition education plan contents.

PENNSYLVANIA DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH Policy Number: 5.01 WIC State Agency USDA Approval Date: February 20, 2024 State Effective Date: April 20, 2024

POLICY MANUAL 5. WIC NUTRITION AND BREASTFEEDING SERVICES. 5.01 Nutrition Education and Counseling.

Page 6 of 6

6. Nutrition Education Coordination Between WIC and External Programs:

a. Local agencies (LAs) are encouraged to coordinate program operations, especially nutrition education activities, with special counseling services and other programs, including but not limited to: Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP), Healthy Beginnings Plus (HBP), Early Intervention, Head Start, teenage pregnancy and parenting projects, family planning, immunization, prenatal and postpartum care, well- child care, dental care, lead testing, smoking, alcohol, and drug abuse counseling, and child abuse counseling. b. The LA shall maintain a working relationship with county Expanded Food and Nutrition Education Program (EFNEP) staff in its WIC Program service area. The local EFNEP contact information shall be included in the LA’s list of referral agencies. c. Coordination with these programs supplements, but does not replace, nutrition education provided by WIC staff, unless approved by the SA.

__________________ References:

1. WIC Regulations: 7 CFR Part 246.11, including 7CFR Part 246.11(a)(3); 7 CFR 246.2. 2. Public Law 108-265, the Child Nutrition and WIC Reauthorization Act of 2004 (June 30, 2004). 3. WIC Nutrition Services Standards, FNS, USDA (August 2013). 4. WIC Program Nutrition Education Guidance (January 2006).

body:
PENNSYLVANIA DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH Policy Number:5.02 WIC State Agency USDA Approval Date: January 28, 2025 State Effective Date: March 29, 2025

POLICY AND PROCEDURE MANUAL 5. Nutrition and Breastfeeding Services 5.02 Breastfeeding Promotion and Support

Page 1 of 7

A. POLICY OVERVIEW

PA WIC must provide breastfeeding education to encourage breastfeeding through a combination of promotion and support activities.

B. POLICY

1. Local agencies (LAs) must institute a strategy for breastfeeding promotion and support for pregnant and breastfeeding participants.

2. LAs must train staff in breastfeeding promotion and/or support in accordance with Policy 3.03, Training of WIC Staff.

3. LAs must provide breastfeeding promotion and support services to participants consistent with State agency (SA) guidance.

4. Provision and Documentation of Breastfeeding Promotion Services:

a. Breastfeeding must be promoted among all pregnant participants to enable an informed infant feeding decision using the following guidelines:

(1) Breastfeeding promotion contacts must inquire about all pregnant participants’ prior knowledge of, experience with, and feelings and attitudes towards breastfeeding by conducting a thorough interview and providing appropriate education to counter any concerns or barriers identified. (2) All pregnant participants must be informed of the contraindications to breastfeeding. (3) Regardless of infant feeding intention prior to conversation with WIC staff, all pregnant participants must receive information describing the advantages of breastfeeding. (4) All pregnant participants must be informed of the differences between breastfeeding, partial breastfeeding, and not breastfeeding woman and infant food packages.

b. LAs must provide participants who are considering or planning to breastfeed with follow-up information, education and counseling throughout their pregnancy. Follow- ups during pregnancy must:

(1) Address individual needs and concerns. (2) Assist participants in making an informed infant feeding decision.

PENNSYLVANIA DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH Policy Number:5.02 WIC State Agency USDA Approval Date: January 28, 2025 State Effective Date: March 29, 2025

POLICY AND PROCEDURE MANUAL 5. Nutrition and Breastfeeding Services 5.02 Breastfeeding Promotion and Support

Page 2 of 7

(3) Assist participants in preparing to successfully breastfeed, including developing a plan to initiate breastfeeding at the hospital and establishing realistic expectations of breastfeeding. (4) Address how family members and peers can support the breastfeeding journey.

c. LAs must document breastfeeding promotion in the MIS in accordance with SA guidance and must include the following:

(1) Prior knowledge and experience with and feelings and attitudes towards breastfeeding. (2) Concerns, barriers, or contraindications to breastfeeding. (3) Infant feeding intentions. (4) Details of breastfeeding education and referrals provided. (5) Plan for follow-up, if needed.

5. Provision and Documentation of Breastfeeding Support Services:

a. LAs must provide adequate support to all breastfeeding participants for the full duration of the breastfeeding journey using the following guidelines:

(1) Breastfeeding management counseling must be based on thorough assessments and with consideration for the breastfeeding dyad’s goals. Refer to B.5.c.-e. in this policy for additional information on breastfeeding-related assessments. (2) Breast pump or breastfeeding aids must be based on a thorough assessment. Refer to section B.7. of this policy for additional information on providing breast pumps and breastfeeding aids. (3) Appropriate food package must be based on breastfeeding status. (4) Supplemental formula must only be provided to the nursing infant in accordance with Policy 5.03, Formula Issuance to Breastfed Infants.

b. Mechanisms for providing support should include: in-clinic contacts, follow-up phone calls by WIC staff (particularly during the critical period in the first 10 days postpartum), peer counselors or lactation consultants, access to breastfeeding helpline, and referrals to breastfeeding support groups.

c. CPA or CPPA must complete an infant feeding screening and assessment at the infant certification and between 4 and 7 months of age and must consist of an evaluation of the infant’s nutritional intake and growth pattern.

PENNSYLVANIA DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH Policy Number:5.02 WIC State Agency USDA Approval Date: January 28, 2025 State Effective Date: March 29, 2025

POLICY AND PROCEDURE MANUAL 5. Nutrition and Breastfeeding Services 5.02 Breastfeeding Promotion and Support

Page 3 of 7

d. A Detailed Breastfeeding Assessment form must be completed when a thorough assessment of the breastfeeding dyad indicates that infant growth is not within normal limits for age or when a breastfeeding problem is reported or identified. The Detailed Breastfeeding Assessment form shall be completed by a CPA, CPPA, BFPC, or any WIC staff who maintain a CLC or IBCLC credential.

(1) Additional follow-up infant feeding screening and assessments and Detailed Breastfeeding Assessments must be conducted at subsequent appointments when a breastfeeding or growth problem is identified.

e. Breastfeeding support and referrals provided must be documented in the MIS in accordance with SA guidance and must include the following information:

(1) Results of the infant feeding screening and assessment. These results include percent of daily nutritional needs being met by supplemental formula, when applicable. (2) Results of the Detailed Breastfeeding Assessment, when applicable. (3) The mother’s breastfeeding plan and goal(s). (4) Any other pertinent information, such as support system, planned follow-up, mother’s commitment level, etc. (5) Plan for follow-up.

6. Purchase and Management of Breast Pumps and Breastfeeding Aids

a. Breast pumps and the parts necessary to operate breast pumps are considered a program benefit and must be provided to participants free of charge when a need has been determined by WIC staff. A variety of breast pump types must be made available through LAs to best support a wide range of participant needs in a cost- effective manner. Refer to section B.7. of this policy for additional details regarding Issuance and Documentation of Breast Pumps and Breastfeeding Aids.

b. LAs must register with the Pennsylvania Department of Health Drugs, Devices, and Cosmetics Program annually to maintain active status as a medical device distributor as breast pumps are considered medical devices.

c. LAs must receive approval from the SA prior to purchasing or renting breast pumps and purchasing breastfeeding aids to ensure all purchases are reasonable, necessary and conform to Federal Regulation and USDA Breastfeeding Policy and Guidance.

d. The amount of breast pumps and breastfeeding aids kept on-site must be reasonable; therefore, breast pumps and breastfeeding aids should be ordered at intervals throughout the year according to current usage.

PENNSYLVANIA DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH Policy Number:5.02 WIC State Agency USDA Approval Date: January 28, 2025 State Effective Date: March 29, 2025

POLICY AND PROCEDURE MANUAL 5. Nutrition and Breastfeeding Services 5.02 Breastfeeding Promotion and Support

Page 4 of 7

e. LAs that purchase their own multi-user, hospital grade electric breast pumps must have a SA-approved procedure in place to retrieve them if participants fail to return them in a timely manner or in damaged condition. Procedures may include phone calls, registered letters, email contacts, use of a collection agency, or more frequent WIC appointments until the breast pump is returned. Breast pumps not returned by a participant that cost WIC more than $1,000.00 will result in a 1-year participant disqualification. Refer to Policy 1.02, Abuse and Fraud Prevention and Investigation.

(1) LAs must not charge a breast pump replacement fee for any breast pumps that have not been returned to the WIC program.

f. LAs that have a rental agreement with a breast pump supplier must follow the procedures of their rental contract when a breast pump has not been returned to WIC at the agreed upon time.

(1) This may include the breast pump supplier seeking reimbursement for the cost of the rental breast pump.

g. WIC Staff responsible for the retrieval of breast pump(s) that have not been returned in a timely manner or have received a breast pump in damaged condition must:

(1) Document all contact attempts to retrieve breast pump(s) in the MIS. (2) Update the status of breast pumps in the MIS to indicate that breast pump(s) have been lost, stolen or damaged after a reasonable effort has been made without success of retrieving the breast pump back into WIC possession or immediately upon receipt of a damaged breast pump. (3) If a breast pump is returned to a local agency or clinic other than the agency or clinic that loaned the pump, the receiving agency or clinic must contact the originating agency or clinic to make arrangements to return the breast pump or, to request a transfer of the breast pump. Upon agreement by both parties, the accepting local agency or clinic must document inventory of this pump and notify the State WIC Office of change.

h. LAs must accurately maintain breast pump inventory in the MIS. Additional inventory efforts are at the discretion of each LA. A count of all breast pumps issued or loaned to participants within each Federal Fiscal Year (FFY) must be submitted to the SA at the end of each FFY.

7. Issuance and Documentation of Breast Pumps and Breastfeeding Aids

PENNSYLVANIA DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH Policy Number:5.02 WIC State Agency USDA Approval Date: January 28, 2025 State Effective Date: March 29, 2025

POLICY AND PROCEDURE MANUAL 5. Nutrition and Breastfeeding Services 5.02 Breastfeeding Promotion and Support

Page 5 of 7

a. Breast pumps and breastfeeding aids may be issued to support breastfeeding success but may not be offered or issued solely as an enticement or incentive to consider or continue breastfeeding.

b. Before offering a breast pump from WIC, staff must determine if the participant’s insurance plan reimburses for breast pumps. If breast pumps are a reimbursable item, staff must refer the individual to their primary insurance provider. However, if the participant must wait an unreasonable amount of time in order to receive a breast pump through the insurance provider or if the insurance provider does not cover a breast pump that is suitable to the participant’s needs, staff may issue a breast pump.

c. Breast pumps and breastfeeding aids may be issued to:

(1) Active participants who have been certified as breastfeeding. i. Exceptions may be approved by the SA on a case-by-case basis. Any approved exceptions must be clearly documented in the MIS. (2) Pregnant participants who are breastfeeding an active WIC infant participant.

d. Participants must receive education from trained, designated staff on the proper assembly, use, and cleaning of breast pumps and parts as well as breastfeeding aids prior to their issuance. Participants must also receive education on safe handling and storage of expressed breast milk at the time of breast pump issuance.

e. All breast pump issuances, information and education provided during the breast pump issuance must be documented in the MIS in accordance with SA guidance.

f. LAs are strongly encouraged to follow-up with participants within 24 hours of breast pump issuance.

g. Signature of the endorser or proxy must be captured in the MIS when issuing serialized breast pumps. When signatures for serialized items cannot be captured in the MIS, the endorser or proxy must sign the Breast Pump Release Form which must be kept on file at the LA.

h. The Breast Pump Release Form must be reviewed with and provided to the endorser or proxy when issuing a serialized breast pump at the time of signature collection.

8. Breastfeeding Supportive Clinic Environment:

PENNSYLVANIA DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH Policy Number:5.02 WIC State Agency USDA Approval Date: January 28, 2025 State Effective Date: March 29, 2025

POLICY AND PROCEDURE MANUAL 5. Nutrition and Breastfeeding Services 5.02 Breastfeeding Promotion and Support

Page 6 of 7

a. LAs must provide a positive clinic environment that is conducive to the promotion and support of breastfeeding through the following means:

(1) Provide educational and promotional materials that portray breastfeeding as the optimal infant feeding method. (2) Does not display formula or materials, displays or logos featuring formula, or images (posters, pictures, brochures, etc.) that feature bottle feeding. However, brochures on formula and bottle feeding may be provided to participants when appropriate. (3) It is the professional responsibility of all staff to promote and support breastfeeding and to refrain from conveying negative attitudes or opinions about breastfeeding regardless of personal viewpoints. (4) The waiting area should be used to promote breastfeeding as the social and cultural norm through signage indicating breastfeeding is welcome anywhere in the LA. (5) LAs must provide a designated supportive environment in which women can breastfeed their infants with more privacy, if desired (i.e. a comfortable breastfeeding area, chairs with arms, etc.). Refer to Policy 1.00, Program Management, for additional information on breastfeeding in the workplace. (6) Staff must not accept complimentary formula for personal use or for distribution to WIC participants.

9. Breastfeeding Coordination Between WIC and External Programs:

a. LAs must contact healthcare providers and community organizations to coordinate breastfeeding promotion efforts that inform other agencies of WIC goals and philosophy regarding breastfeeding.

b. Coordination with external programs and community organizations may supplement, but not replace, breastfeeding services provided by WIC staff, unless approved by the SA.

c. LAs are encouraged to establish or participate in a local breastfeeding coalition or task force to help promote breastfeeding in its service area.

10. Breastfeeding Plans:

a. LAs must develop and submit to the SA an annual breastfeeding plan in accordance with guidance distributed by the SA.

b. Annual breastfeeding plans must be prepared by the Breastfeeding Coordinator. When feasible, all staff that provide breastfeeding promotion and support services

PENNSYLVANIA DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH Policy Number:5.02 WIC State Agency USDA Approval Date: January 28, 2025 State Effective Date: March 29, 2025

POLICY AND PROCEDURE MANUAL 5. Nutrition and Breastfeeding Services 5.02 Breastfeeding Promotion and Support

Page 7 of 7

should be given the opportunity to participate in the development of the LA breastfeeding plan.

c. All staff that provides breastfeeding promotion and support services must be familiar with Federal and SA requirements for breastfeeding services and must be familiar with the LA breastfeeding plan contents.

References: 1. WIC Regulations. 7 CFR 246.2 (Participant Violation) 2. WIC Regulations. 7 CFR 246.11 3. WIC Regulations. 7 CFR 246.14(b)(1)(iii) 4. USDA WIC Breastfeeding Policy and Guidance. (July 2016) 5. Pennsylvania Department of Health Drugs, Devices, and Cosmetics Program: Drugs, Devices and Cosmetics Program (pa.gov)

Policy Status: 1. This Policy supersedes Policy Number 5.02 dated February 13, 2017.

PENNSYLVANIA DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH

Policy Number: 5.03 WIC State Agency

USDA Approval Date: March 5, 2025

State Effective Date: May 5, 2025

POLICY MANUAL

5. NUTRITION AND BREASTFEEDING SERVICES.

5.03 Formula Issuance to Breastfed Infants.

Page 1 of 2

A. POLICY OVERVIEW:

PA WIC shall provide supplementation to breastfed infants when clinically indicated due to questionable or inadequate intake, a breastfeeding or medical problem, or an assessed need indicates supplemental formula is nutritionally necessary.

B. POLICY:

1. All formula issued to breastfeeding participants shall be handled by Competent Professional Authorities (CPAs) or Competent Paraprofessional Authorities (CPPAs) who have successfully completed appropriate breastfeeding training. Refer to Policy 3.03, Training of WIC Staff.

2. If a mother needs or wants to supplement breastfeeding, appropriate WIC staff (such as Designated Breastfeeding Experts (DBEs), CPAs, CPPAs, or Breastfeeding Peer Counselors) shall first provide education about the option of milk expression and encourage supplementation with expressed breast milk. As needed, appropriate WIC staff shall inform the participant of the impacts on health and milk supply that are associated with formula introduction.

a. If needed, LAs shall issue a WIC breast pump to enable milk expression for supplementation purposes. Refer to Policy 5.02, Breastfeeding Promotion and Support. b. LAs shall provide information about the enhanced food package for fully breastfeeding women and infants.

3. Prior to issuing supplemental formula, WIC staff must identify the reason for formula introduction and determine if a Detailed Breastfeeding Assessment and/or additional breastfeeding support is needed. Detailed Breastfeeding Assessments shall be conducted as outlined in Policy 5.02, Breastfeeding Promotion and Support.

4. If the infant feeding screening and assessment, conducted by a CPA or CPPA, deems it nutritionally necessary to supplement with formula, no more than 104 reconstituted fluid ounces may be issued to breastfed infants who are less than one month old at the time of benefit issuance.

a. LAs shall provide breastfeeding parents who request formula prior to the infant’s first month with in-depth breastfeeding support according to the protocols in SA guidance. b. Additionally, as appropriate, LAs shall refer such breastfeeding parents to a peer counselor, WIC Designated Breastfeeding Expert, lactation consultant, breastfeeding coordinator and/or another lactation specialist available at the local agency or in the community.

5. For infants one month or older, the amount of formula issued shall be based on assessed need. The mother’s food package will be based on the amount of formula prescribed in the infant’s food package. Refer to Policy 5.06, Issuance of Food Packages.

a. If the mother requests more formula than the infant feeding screening and

PENNSYLVANIA DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH

Policy Number: 5.03 WIC State Agency

USDA Approval Date: March 5, 2025

State Effective Date: May 5, 2025

POLICY MANUAL

5. NUTRITION AND BREASTFEEDING SERVICES.

5.03 Formula Issuance to Breastfed Infants.

Page 2 of 2

assessment indicates, CPAs or CPPAs shall inform the mother of the amount of formula WIC will provide. CPAs and CPPAs shall also inform the mother that feeding formula above the nutritional needs of the infant can result in overfeeding, vomiting, stomach and bowel discomfort, infant/child obesity and may decrease breast milk supply.

6. If supplemental formula is being offered to the infant:

a. CPAs, CPPAs, or DBEs must inform the participant of the percent of daily nutritional needs being met by formula. The percent of daily nutritional needs and the reason for supplementing with formula shall also be documented in the MIS. b. CPAs and CPPAs must inform the participant of safe formula preparation, handling and storage per manufacturer instructions. This education must be documented in the MIS per SA guidance.

7. Supplemental formula shall be issued in powder or concentrate forms. Ready-to-feed (RTF) formula may only be issued to supplement breastfeeding when the criteria outlined in Policy 5.08, Infant Formula, have been met. Staff must obtain the appropriate medical documentation and document in the MIS the details outlined in Policy 5.08, Infant Formula.

__________________________ Reference(s): 1. WIC Regulations: 7 CFR 246.10(e)(1)(ii) 2. WIC Regulations: 7 CFR 246.10(e)(2) 3. WIC Breastfeeding Policy and Guidance, FNS, USDA (July 2016).

Policy Status: 1. This Policy supersedes Policy Number 7.06 dated June 29, 2015.

PENNSYLVANIA DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH Policy Number: 5.04 WIC State Agency USDA Approval Date: February 20, 2024 State Effective Date: April 20, 2024

POLICY MANUAL

5. NUTRITION AND BREASTFEEDING SERVICES

5.04 Breastfeeding Peer Counselor Program.

Page 1 of 5

A. POLICY OVERVIEW

The PA WIC Breastfeeding Peer Counselor (BFPC) Program shall operate in accordance with this policy to provide counseling, support, and other services which encourage breastfeeding for WIC participants. The requirements in this policy pertain to local agencies (LAs) that receive specific Peer Counselor Program funding. LAs that choose to operate a BFPC Program using Nutrition Services Administration (NSA) funds shall operate the program according to this policy to the best of their ability.

B. POLICY

1. BFPC Program Purpose and Management

a. The BFPC Program supports normal breastfeeding by providing basic breastfeeding information and encouragement to pregnant and breastfeeding WIC participants. BFPC services support a successful breastfeeding journey through mother-to-mother relationships and frequent communication and referrals to appropriate WIC or external professionals for complex breastfeeding challenges per State agency (SA) guidance. b. The BFPC Program shall be operated by a BFPC and managed by a BFPC Supervisor. A Senior BFPC is an optional position to allow LAs to offer a career ladder for BFPC staff. Refer to Policy 3.02, Local Agency Staffing, for staffing recommendations and required qualifications, experience, duties, and skills for all BFPC Program positions. c. A BFPC Supervisor: (1) Shall monitor BFPCs to ensure BFPC program requirements are met, consistency of services and to confirm that the support offered is professional, confidential, and accurate as well as to provide encouragement and positive feedback. (2) Shall develop partnerships with stakeholders in the area to help establish a referral system as well as promote the BFPC program within the community. These partnerships may include but are not limited to; local breastfeeding coalitions, La Leche League or other local breastfeeding support groups, hospital lactation consultants, Early Head Start, Healthy Beginnings Plus, and Cooperative Extension. These partners will be given the opportunity to support the program by: a) Taking referrals from BFPCs. b) Providing an in-service for BFPCs. c) Promoting the program with health care providers. d) Referring clients to the program. e) Providing a breastfeeding support group.

PENNSYLVANIA DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH Policy Number: 5.04 WIC State Agency USDA Approval Date: February 20, 2024 State Effective Date: April 20, 2024

POLICY MANUAL

5. NUTRITION AND BREASTFEEDING SERVICES

5.04 Breastfeeding Peer Counselor Program.

Page 2 of 5

d. LAs must train BFPC Program staff upon hire according to Policy 3.03, Training of WIC Staff. In addition to the completion of required trainings, BFPC Program staff shall also receive continuing education and support through: (1) LA staff in-services. a) As part of the WIC team, BFPCs are required to attend any in-services scheduled by the LA. (2) Relevant trainings provided by the SA. (3) Weekly phone and email updates with supervisor. (4) BFPC meetings and in-services. (5) Additional trainings as determined by the LA.

e. BFPCs may obtain specific job-related certifications such as Certified Lactation Counselor (CLC); however, BFPCs may not hold a higher credential such as, but not limited to, International Board-Certified Lactation Consultant (IBCLC), which exceeds the qualifications and job responsibilities of a BFPC. (1) BFPCs holding a CLC credential must remain within the BFPC scope of practice as per Section 2 of this policy, Provision of BFPC Program Services. (2) LAs may provide career ladder options for BFPCs who wish to further their education.

f. BFPCs cannot provide peer counselor services to mothers who are not certified on WIC but may educate non-WIC mothers about the WIC Program and encourage them to apply for WIC benefits. (1) If a non-WIC mother needs immediate breastfeeding support, WIC BFPCs shall provide referrals to external breastfeeding resources in the community.

g. BFPC Program Staff shall record hours worked on weekly time sheet. (1) If BFPCs also function as a Program Assistant or clerical staff, the time sheets must document BFPC hours separately for invoicing purposes. Where possible, BFPCs also functioning as a Program Assistant or clerical staff should not perform other WIC duties related to certification and program eligibility determination as this would compromise the unique peer-to-peer relationship. (2) Staff who hold the BFPC or Senior BFPC position shall not also function as a CPA or CPPA regardless of funding source or schedule.

h. BFPC funds may only be used for expenses authorized under the USDA BFPC Program. All receipts for BFPC expenses and staffing time sheets must be maintained for fiscal audit purposes. SA will distribute the Allowable Costs for Breastfeeding Peer Counselor Fund Chart document as provided by USDA.

PENNSYLVANIA DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH Policy Number: 5.04 WIC State Agency USDA Approval Date: February 20, 2024 State Effective Date: April 20, 2024

POLICY MANUAL

5. NUTRITION AND BREASTFEEDING SERVICES

5.04 Breastfeeding Peer Counselor Program.

Page 3 of 5

i. Expenses which are allowed under BFPC funds may also be funded through NSA funding if it is a WIC allowable purchase in accordance with Policy 2.02, Cost Allowability for Travel, Incentive Items, Tuition Reimbursement, and Renovations, and SA Guidance.

2. Provision of BFPC Program Services a. LAs must adhere to the scope of practice for all BFPC Program positions as defined by SA guidance.

b. BFPCs shall: (1) provide breastfeeding contacts using interactive counseling techniques at specific, required time frames before and after delivery based on SA guidance. (2) discuss topics related to stages of pregnancy or postpartum based on anticipatory guidance, assessment and participant needs. (3) document all contacts in the MIS based on SA guidance.

c. BFPCs counsel WIC mothers at the WIC clinic, by phone, by virtual platform, or during hospital or home visits as determined by the LA. Method of communication shall be documented in the MIS in addition to other required documentation set forth by the SA.

d. Each LA must develop a tracking system that BFPCs can use to contact participants within the required time frames. Suggested methods for tracking include but are not limited to: (1) Schedule participants in MIS scheduler under a BFPC column based on Next Contact Date. (2) Virtual work calendar where the participants’ Family ID Numbers (FIDs) and/or Participant ID Numbers (PIDs) names are added on the date and time they should be contacted. Names shall not be displayed on a virtual work calendar to protect the privacy of the participant(s). Names, phone numbers, and birthdate shall not be displayed on a virtual work calendar to protect the privacy of the participant(s). See Policy 1.04, Confidentiality of Participant Records. (3) Microsoft Access or similar database utilization. (4) Cardex system where participant names are filed according to the date they must be contacted.

e. BFPCs must have email and texting capability to contact participants who require or prefer this method of communication.

f. BFPCs must maintain strict confidentiality of participant records where permission is granted in the MIS for phone, voicemail, and/or text message contact. Refer to Policy 1.04, Confidentiality of Participant Records, and SA guidance.

PENNSYLVANIA DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH Policy Number: 5.04 WIC State Agency USDA Approval Date: February 20, 2024 State Effective Date: April 20, 2024

POLICY MANUAL

5. NUTRITION AND BREASTFEEDING SERVICES

5.04 Breastfeeding Peer Counselor Program.

Page 4 of 5

g. BFPCs shall provide accurate, up-to-date breastfeeding information based on the PA WIC Breastfeeding Manual and standardized trainings.

h. BFPCs will refer participants with breastfeeding challenges to the BFPC Supervisor, Designated Breastfeeding Expert (DBE), and/or the LA Breastfeeding Coordinator for immediate follow-up. (1) If none are available, the BFPC will contact other lactation experts in their area from the Breastfeeding Referral Guide that is provided by the SA. The BFPC Supervisor shall update this list as requested.

i. BFPCs shall respond to any calls from participants on the same working day. (1) If there is no BFPC available, the call will be forwarded to the BFPC Supervisor or LA Breastfeeding Coordinator. (2) BFPCs shall also provide participants with a number they can call after hours in case of emergencies. This may be a cell phone provided by the LA, a number connected to voicemail which will be routinely checked by the BFPCs, or use of the WIC Breastfeeding Helpline. (3) BFPCs can determine what times are suitable for participants to call or to check voicemails. Although providing 24-hour emergency coverage would be ideal, BFPCs should, at a minimum, be available until 9:00 PM on weekdays and Saturdays and Sundays until 1:00 PM, except for holidays.

j. BFPCs shall respond to any referrals from outside sources within 24 hours or the next business day. (1) If there is no BFPC available, the referral will be forwarded to the BFPC Supervisor or LA Breastfeeding Coordinator. (2) If a referred patient is not a WIC participant, the BFPC shall forward the patient’s information to a WIC LA staff member for WIC eligibility determination and certification.

k. To generate more referrals to WIC from healthcare providers, a letter or informational packet shall be provided announcing the availability of breastfeeding services for their patients.

l. To further increase program awareness, the BFPC will follow-up using a BFPC consult notes form to keep providers informed of breastfeeding services provided to their patients. Before providing any information to the physician, participants must sign a release form in accordance with Policy 1.04, Confidentiality of Participant Records.

PENNSYLVANIA DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH Policy Number: 5.04 WIC State Agency USDA Approval Date: February 20, 2024 State Effective Date: April 20, 2024

POLICY MANUAL

5. NUTRITION AND BREASTFEEDING SERVICES

5.04 Breastfeeding Peer Counselor Program.

Page 5 of 5

__________________ References: 1. USDA BFPC Management Guide (July 2016) 2. WIC Breastfeeding Model Components for Peer Counseling 3. USDA Breastfeeding Policy and Guidance (July 2016) 4. Nutrition Service Standards: Standard 9 Breastfeeding Peer Counseling (August 2013) 5. Allowable Costs for Breastfeeding Peer Counselor Fund Chart (as provided annually)

PENNSYLVANIA DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH

Policy Number: 5.05 WIC State Agency USDA Approval Date: November 8, 2023

State Effective Date: January 7, 2024

POLICY MANUAL

5. NUTRITION AND BREASTFEEDING SERVICES.

5.05. Authorized Product List (APL) and Statewide Food List.

Page 1 of 2

A. POLICY OVERVIEW:

The PA WIC State agency (SA) will review and approve foods for inclusion in the program and create a standard statewide food list that will be reviewed every five years and updated yearly as appropriate. The SA will also be responsible for maintaining the Authorized Product List (APL) which is a list of all approved Universal Product Codes (UPCs).

B. POLICY:

1. The SA will:

a. Utilize federal and state regulations and standards to determine inclusion of food products in the statewide food list and APL.

b. Conduct the food list application process for food manufacturers every five years. In interim years, the SA will consider changes to the statewide food list based on criteria that includes, but is not limited to the following:

(1) Federal law, regulations, and guidance currently in effect. (2) State contracts in effect. (3) Changes in the type and nutrient level of foods currently authorized by the USDA. (4) Information on new products received since the last revision of the list.

c. Develop and maintain a standard statewide food list which will be published annually in English and Spanish.

d. Make changes in the statewide food list as required as a result of product reformulation, problems of product safety, or product availability. SA will notify local agencies (LAs) and vendors at the time such changes occur.

e. Update the APL for missing or discontinued items based on information submitted by vendors, participants, or LA staff using the WICShopper app or email.

2. The LAs shall:

a. Adhere to the current statewide food list as published by the SA.

b. Not add to or delete items from the list except as directed by the SA.

c. Submit information to SA concerning missing or discontinued items for purposes of keeping APL accurate.

d. Instruct each participant, endorser, or proxy on the details of foods allowed and not allowed according to the current statewide food list, WICShopper app, and the proper use of food instruments to obtain allowable foods.

PENNSYLVANIA DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH

PENNSYLVANIA DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH

Policy Number: 5.06 WIC State Agency USDA Approval Date: November 8, 2023 State Effective Date: January 7, 2024

POLICY MANUAL

5. NUTRITION AND BREASTFEEDING SERVICES.

5.06. Issuance of Food Packages.

Page 1 of 4

A. POLICY OVERVIEW:

The Pennsylvania Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants and Children (PA WIC) shall prescribe authorized supplemental foods to eligible participants according to food packages established by USDA. Proration, reissuance, and card balance corrections shall occur based on certain circumstances.

B. DEFINITIONS:

a. Breastfeeding Woman: A woman who breastfeeds at least once a day.

b. Partially Breastfeeding Part In: A woman who is breastfeeding an infant but also partially formula feeding the infant up to the maximum allowance described for partially (mostly) breastfed infants.

c. Partially Breastfeeding Part Out: A woman who is breastfeeding an infant but also partially formula feeding the infant over the maximum allowance described for partially (mostly) breastfed infants.

C. POLICY:

1. Authorized Food Packages:

a. Supplemental foods shall be provided as a benefit to participants on WIC in an effort to address current public health concerns.

b. Authorized supplemental foods shall be prescribed according to category, risk and nutritional needs of the participant based on their WIC type on the first of the month:

(1) Food Package I -- Infants 0 through 5 months. (2) Food Package II -- Infants 6 through 11 months. (3) Food Package III – Women, Infants and Children with qualifying conditions. (4) Food Package IV -- Children 12 months and up to age 5. (5) Food Package V – Pregnant, Pregnant and Partially Breastfeeding (Part Out), and Partially Breastfeeding (Part In) Women. (6) Food Package VI – Not Breastfeeding Postpartum Women and Partially Breastfeeding (Part Out) Women. (7) Food Package VII -- Fully Breastfeeding Women, Pregnant Women of Multiples, Pregnant Women Fully Breastfeeding or Partially Breastfeeding (Part In) an infant and Partially Breastfeeding Women (Part In) of Multiples. (8) Food Package VII+ -- Fully Breastfeeding Women of Multiples.

c. The maximum monthly amounts of supplemental foods permitted for each WIC category of participants shall not be exceeded. Refer to State agency (SA) guidance on maximum monthly amounts.

PENNSYLVANIA DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH

Policy Number: 5.06 WIC State Agency USDA Approval Date: November 8, 2023 State Effective Date: January 7, 2024

POLICY MANUAL

5. NUTRITION AND BREASTFEEDING SERVICES.

5.06. Issuance of Food Packages.

Page 2 of 4

d. At least one authorized food in each food category shall be available to participants. For more specific information, refer to Policy 5.07, Food Package Tailoring.

2. Issuance of Food Packages:

a. Infants: (1) The infant’s package is determined by the breastfeeding description and information gathered in the Management Information System (MIS).

b. Pregnant Women: (1) The local agency (LA) staff must encourage the pregnant woman to report the birth of her child to the LA within the month of delivery. (2) A pregnant woman is entitled to her last month of Food Instruments (FIs) any time after her date of delivery but no later than six weeks after delivery.

c. Postpartum Women: (1) A postpartum not breastfeeding woman may apply for WIC benefits any time after her date of delivery but no later than six months after delivery. (2) A postpartum, breastfeeding woman may apply for WIC benefits any time after her date of delivery but no later than the infant's first birthday. (3) A multiparous breastfeeding woman can receive Food Package VII if the infants are Partially Breastfeeding (Part In) or at least one of the infants is not receiving any formula. All other partially breastfeeding women of multiples are eligible to receive Food Package V.

d. Children: (1) Children are entitled for benefits from age one until the last day of the month of their fifth birthday.

3. Proration of Food Packages:

a. The Management Information System (MIS) automatically determines proration for the current month. Prorated food packages could be issued to participants when the following temporary situations occur:

(1) Initial participants who come in later in the month and need benefits to reach the beginning of the next month. (2) Participants who have missed picking up their benefits for the current month. (3) Pregnant women being recertified as fully breast feeding after delivery who have already received benefits in the last 30 days that did not include their additional foods.

PENNSYLVANIA DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH

Policy Number: 5.06 WIC State Agency USDA Approval Date: November 8, 2023 State Effective Date: January 7, 2024

POLICY MANUAL

5. NUTRITION AND BREASTFEEDING SERVICES.

5.06. Issuance of Food Packages.

Page 3 of 4

b. The MIS will prorate food packages based on the number of days in the month when 2/3 or 1/3 of the packages will be given. See table below:

Dates of Proration for all Food Packages # of Days in Month Full Package 2/3 Package 1/3 Package 28 Days 1st – 8th 9th – 18th 19th – 28th 29 Days 1st – 9th 10th – 19th 20th – 29th 30 Days 1st – 10th 11th – 20th 21st – 30th 31 Days 1st – 11th 12th – 21st 22nd – 31st

c. When food packages have been prorated, LA staff shall explain the reason(s) for the proration to the endorser.

d. Reasonable efforts shall be made to reschedule missed appointments as soon as possible so proration is not necessary.

4. Reissuance of Food Packages:

a. Prior to reissuing food benefits, LA staff must: (1) Document any returned formula in the MIS. (2) Update the food package, if applicable.

b. Redeemed or expired benefits cannot be reissued.

c. Use Reissue to Original when formula has been returned on a date when proration occurs. See table above.

5. Card Balance Correction:

a. The LA shall monitor the Card Balance Correction report monthly to make sure staff are not over issuing or fraud is not occurring.

b. Over issuance may occur in the following situations: (1) When the WIC card has been documented as stolen (2) When the WIC card has been documented as lost (3) When there is a change of custody or foster care (4) When the WIC foods have been destroyed by a documented fire or natural disaster (5) When system errors or other situations occur, contact the SA or help desk.

PENNSYLVANIA DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH

PENNSYLVANIA DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH

Policy Number: 5.07 WIC State Agency USDA Approval Date: November 8, 2023 State Effective Date: January 7, 2024

POLICY MANUAL ____________________________________________________________________________________ 5. NUTRITION AND BREASTFEEDING SERVICES.

5.07 Food Package Tailoring.

Page 1 of 3

A. POLICY OVERVIEW:

Pennsylvania Women, Infants and Children (WIC) program shall authorize Competent Professional Authorities (CPAs) and Competent Paraprofessional Authorities (CPPAs) to prescribe and tailor food packages to assure participants receive the maximum amounts of allowable foods.

B. POLICY:

1. Only CPAs and CPPAs who have been trained and authorized by the State agency (SA) may prescribe and tailor food packages. Refer to Policy 3.02, Local Agency Staffing, to determine qualifications for WIC staff.

2. Food package tailoring is based upon providing the maximum amounts of allowable foods and tailoring as needed. Food packages are based on participant WIC type, breastfeeding status, and age. Participants must be offered at least one food from each food category for which they are eligible on the first of the month. The exceptions to this requirement are:

a. The participant declines any of the foods offered in the food package; and b. The participant has medical and/or developmental problems, which warrant excluding a particular food category or item. c. Food may be reduced or eliminated based on assessment, including religious and cultural needs. See B.9 below.

All above exceptions shall be documented in the MIS.

3. When tailoring food packages, CPAs or CPPAs shall individualize the quantity of food provided from each WIC category and determine the specific types within food subcategories. One food category cannot be completely substituted for another. Any tailoring cannot exceed the maximum monthly levels established by Federal Regulations. For instance, additional juice above the maximum allowed cannot be substituted for milk in the case of milk intolerance.

4. Whole milk is the standard milk for issuance to 1-year-old children (12 through 23 months old). Fat-reduced (2%, 1% or nonfat) milks may be issued to 1-year-old children for whom overweight or obesity is a concern. The need for fat-reduced milks for 1-year-old children must be based on an individual nutritional assessment and documented in the MIS. For children receiving Food Package III, medical documentation must be obtained before tailoring to fat-reduced milks.

5. Lowfat (1%) or nonfat milks are the standard milk for issuance to children (24 months or older) and women. Reduced fat (2%) milk is authorized only for participants with certain conditions, including but not limited to, underweight and maternal weight loss during pregnancy. The need for reduced fat (2%) milk for children (24 months or older), under Food Package IV, and women, under Food Packages V-VII, must be based on an individual nutritional assessment and documented in the MIS.

PENNSYLVANIA DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH

Policy Number: 5.07 WIC State Agency USDA Approval Date: November 8, 2023 State Effective Date: January 7, 2024

POLICY MANUAL ____________________________________________________________________________________ 5. NUTRITION AND BREASTFEEDING SERVICES.

5.07 Food Package Tailoring.

Page 2 of 3

6. Food packages for children (24 months or older) and women may only be tailored to whole milk when issued Food Package III and with medical documentation.

7. The SA retains exclusive authority to make administrative adjustments to contain food package costs. LA staff shall not tailor food packages solely to lower cost.

8. The SA and LAs shall monitor all food package tailoring procedures through program reviews.

9. Prior to prescribing and tailoring food packages, WIC staff shall conduct a Value Enhanced Nutrition Assessment (VENA). Communicate with participant/caregiver/healthcare providers as needed. Gather the following information:

a. Participant’s personal preference and cultural eating patterns. b. Participant’s age and developmental stage. c. Available household food storage and preparation equipment. d. Ability of the participant or caregiver to prepare food/formula. e. Participant’s nutritional and medical needs (i.e. food allergies/intolerances).

10. Review participants’ food packages periodically using criteria in section B.9. above to determine if they are still appropriate. Review may occur:

a. At recertification and health evaluation appointments for all relevant WIC types; b. When infants reach 6 months of age; c. When infants turn one year of age; d. When pregnant women are certified as postpartum; e. When a pregnant breastfeeding woman stops breastfeeding her fully or partially (Part In) breastfed infant; or when that infant turns one year of age. f. When breastfeeding women request to receive infant formula; g. When breastfeeding infants are receiving supplemental formula; h. When a physician documents a need for change; i. At the request of a participant; and j. At the WIC staff's discretion.

11. When tailoring food packages for homeless participants, or those living in temporary accommodations such as shelters or other group residential settings, consider the cooking and food storage facilities available to the participant at the facility itself or elsewhere.

Reference(s): 1. WIC Regulations: 7 CFR Part 246.10. 2. USDA Food Package Policy & Guidance (March 2018)

PENNSYLVANIA DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH

Policy Number: 5.08 WIC State Agency USDA Approval Date: November 8, 2023 State Effective Date: January 7, 2024

POLICY MANUAL

5. NUTRITION AND BREASTFEEDING SERVICES.

5.08. Infant Formula.

Page 1 of 3

A. POLICY OVERVIEW:

Pursuant to 42 U.S.C 1786(h)(8)(A)(i), the Pennsylvania Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants and Children (PA WIC) uses a competitive bidding system to procure infant formula. PA WIC uses a “single solicitation,” “single-supplier” competitive bidding system.

B. DEFINITIONS:

a. Infant Formula: As defined in Section 201(z) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act, as amended by the Infant Formula Act of 1980 (Pub. L. 96–359), (FDCA), infant formula is “a food which purports to be or is represented for special dietary use solely as a food for infants by reason of its simulation of human milk or its suitability as a complete or partial substitute for human milk.” 21 U.S.C. 321(z). U.S. Food and Drug Administration’s (FDA) regulations, 21 CFR, 105.3(e), mirror WIC definitions of an infant as persons not more than 12 months old.

b. Exempt Formula: As defined by Section 412 of the FDCA, an exempt infant formula is “[a]ny infant formula which is represented and labeled for use by an infant-- (A) who has an inborn error of metabolism or low birth weight, or (B) who otherwise has an unusual medical or dietary problem[.]” 21 U.S.C. 350a(h)(1). See Policy 5.10, Exempt Infant Formula and WIC-Eligible Nutritionals, for more information.

c. Contract Formula: Any infant formula that is provided to WIC participants through a rebate contract negotiated with an infant formula manufacturer.

(1) Primary Infant Formula: Defined as “[t]he specific infant formula for which manufacturers submit a bid to a State agency in response to a rebate solicitation and for which a contract is awarded by the State agency as a result of that bid.” 7 CFR 246.2;

(2) Alternate Infant Formula: any cow’s milk based or partially hydrolyzed formula (including lactose free formula and formula with added rice starch) intended for feeding infants who may have conditions as noted in section C.5.

d. Non-Contract Formula: Any standard infant formula that is not covered by a rebate contract as described above.

C. POLICY:

1. A Competent Professional Authority (CPA) or a Competent Paraprofessional Authority (CPPA) shall be responsible for prescribing formula in Food Packages I and II. Refer to Policy 5.10, Exempt Infant Formula and WIC-Eligible Nutritionals, for prescribing formula in Food Package III.

2. Formulas shall be provided as concentrated liquid or powder. RTF formula may be authorized when the CPA determines a need as described in Section C.8.

3. Primary Infant Formula shall be provided as a first choice for infants requiring standard

PENNSYLVANIA DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH

Policy Number: 5.08 WIC State Agency USDA Approval Date: November 8, 2023 State Effective Date: January 7, 2024

POLICY MANUAL

5. NUTRITION AND BREASTFEEDING SERVICES.

5.08. Infant Formula.

Page 2 of 3

formula.

4. An Alternate Infant Formula falls under the contracted infant formulas and may be provided to accommodate a variety of infant conditions that include, but are not limited to: documented infant formula intolerances, food allergies, or inappropriate growth patterns that do not require the use of an exempt infant formula. Medical documentation may be needed.

5. Prescriptions may be faxed or provided electronically to the local agency or clinic. Verbal orders for Alternate Infant Formulas can be accepted by a CPA on a case-by-case basis. Written confirmation of the medical documentation must be obtained within one month after the phone call.

6. Once all appropriate Contract Formulas have been ruled out, Non-Contract Formula may be issued only when a Contract Formula would place the participant at medical risk because of a diagnosed condition as indicated on appropriate medical documentation. These instances must be approved by the SA on a case-by-case basis.

7. Refer participants to their physician before switching from milk-based to soy-based formula or vice versa.

a. Symptoms such as vomiting, diarrhea, or excessive gas may be caused by medical problems or inappropriate feeding practices rather than formula intolerance.

b. Many infants who are allergic to milk-based formulas are also allergic to soy and require a protein hydrolysate formula. Refer to Policy 5.10, Exempt Infant Formulas and WIC-Eligible Nutritionals.

c. Soy formulas are not appropriate for pre-term infants.

8. Provide RTF formula only when:

a. There is an unsanitary or restricted water supply; or

b. The participant's caregiver may have difficulty in correctly preparing the concentrated liquid or powder formula.

c. The formula is available in RTF only.

d. Powder is the only alternative to RTF formula and the infant is immunocompromised or at risk of infection from powder formula. Infants should be monitored monthly.

e. If a participant is experiencing homelessness or living in a shelter.

f. Additionally, the following justifications may be used to issue RTF formula in Food Package III:

(1) If a RTF formula better accommodates the participant’s condition.

PENNSYLVANIA DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH

Policy Number: 5.08 WIC State Agency USDA Approval Date: November 8, 2023 State Effective Date: January 7, 2024

POLICY MANUAL

5. NUTRITION AND BREASTFEEDING SERVICES.

5.08. Infant Formula.

Page 3 of 3

(2) If it improves the participant’s compliance in consuming the prescribed WIC formula.

g. Document the reason for providing RTF formula in the Management Information System (MIS). Written documentation from the health care provider is needed as justification.

9. Infant formulas may be provided to non-breastfed infants and breastfed infants who need supplemental formula. Refer to Policy 5.03, Formula Issuance for Breastfed Infants.

a. Infant formulas may be provided to children when a physician’s prescription justifies the need, as described in Policy 5.10, Exempt Infant Formula and WIC-Eligible Nutritionals.

WIC Regulations: 7 CFR subparts 246.2; 246.10, including 246.10(e)(1)(iii); 246.16a. 4. Federal Food Drug and Cosmetic Act; Section 201 21 USC 321(z); Section 412, Section 350a (h)(1) 5. 21 CFR 105.3 6. USDA WIC Policy Memorandum #2014-1A, Clarification on Medical Documentation for Infant Formula Issued in Food Packages I and II (January 7, 2014)

PENNSYLVANIA DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH Policy Number: 5.09 WIC State Agency

USDA Approval Date: November 8, 2023 State Effective Date: January 7, 2024

POLICY MANUAL

5. NUTRITION AND BREASTFEEDING SERVICES.

5.09 Returned Formula Inventory.

Page 1 of 1

A. POLICY OVERVIEW:

PA WIC shall operate a Formula Return Register to track formulas being returned by participants as a result of switching formulas or no longer needing formula.

B. POLICY:

1. Formula returns shall be made only at the local agency/clinic and not at the retail store unless directed by the state agency (SA).

2. Participants shall return any unused and unopened formula when requesting a formula change.

a. Staff shall record any returned formula in the MIS for current month purchases prior to creating the new food package. b. Staff shall record returned formula on the Formula Return Register. c. Staff shall not reissue returned formula to another participant unless directed by the SA.

3. A documented inventory of all returned and donated formula shall be maintained by the local agency for each clinic location.

a. Discard expired, damaged, dented or rusted cans of formula. b. Returned formula may be donated to a local food pantry/bank at any time, preferably with a minimum of 30 days remaining prior to the expiration date. c. Document the disposition of the formula on the Formula Return Register.

4. The local agency shall:

a. Check formula inventory once a month to reconcile the formula in storage with formula listed on the Formula Return Register. b. Donate formula that is about to expire. c. Discard formula that has expired.

5. Direct ship formulas which are shipped to a WIC clinic and not picked up by the intended participant can be reissued to another participant. These products shall be listed on the Formula Return Register. MIS messages can be utilized to notify other local WIC agencies that the formula is available. The message shall include the formula name, amount, the contact person and the phone number. If another local agency is able to use the formula, ship it to the agency and record that on the Formula Return Register. Update the MIS message as needed.

6. Shipping charges, from the shipping LA, can be submitted on their monthly WIC invoice.

Policy Status: 1. This Policy supersedes Policy Number 7.07, dated May 21, 2015.

PENNSYLVANIA DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH

Policy Number: 5.10 WIC State Agency USDA Approval Date: March 5, 2025 State Effective Date: May 5, 2025

POLICY MANUAL

5. NUTRITION AND BREASTFEEDING SERVICES.

5.10 Exempt Infant Formula and WIC-Eligible Nutritionals

Page 1 of 4 A. POLICY OVERVIEW:

Pennsylvania Women, Infants and Children (PA WIC) must issue infant formula, exempt infant formula or WIC-eligible Nutritionals to woman, infant or child participants with a documented qualifying condition.

B. DEFINITIONS:

Exempt Infant Formula: As defined by Section 412 of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (21 U.S.C. 350a(h)), an exempt infant formula is “[a]ny infant formula which is represented and labeled for use by an infant—(A) who has an inborn error of metabolism or a low birth weight, or (B) who otherwise has an unusual medical or dietary problem[.]” 21 USC 350a(h)(1)(A)-(B).

Phenylketonuria (PKU): Persons with phenylketonuria (PKU) cannot metabolize the amino acid phenylalanine. Such individuals must restrict dietary protein to prevent toxic accumulation of phenylalanine that can cause intellectual and developmental disabilities and neurological problems. Participants with PKU require formulas that are free of phenylalanine. Participants with PKU receive medical care, diet prescription and nutritional counseling at one of the following state contracted PKU Treatment Centers (PTCs) in Pennsylvania: Children’s Hospital of Philadelphia, St. Christopher's Hospital for Children in Philadelphia, Children's Hospital of Pittsburgh, Geisinger Medical Center, or Hershey Medical Center. Follow-up care is provided by community health nurses and the metabolic dietitian at the PTCs. The PKU Treatment Centers refer potentially eligible PKU patients to the PA WIC Program.

WIC-Eligible Nutritionals (WEN): “certain enteral products that are specifically formulated and commercially manufactured (as opposed to a naturally occurring foodstuff used in its natural state) to provide nutritional support for individuals with a qualifying condition, when the use of conventional foods is precluded, restricted, or inadequate. Such WIC-eligible nutritionals must serve the purpose of a food, meal, or diet (may be nutritionally complete or incomplete) and provide a source of calories and one or more nutrients; be designed for enteral digestion via an oral or tube feeding; and may not be a conventional food, drug, flavoring, or enzyme. WIC-eligible nutritionals include many, but not all, products that meet the definition of medical food in section 5(b)(3) of the Orphan Drug Act (21 U.S.C. 360ee(b)(3)).

C. POLICY:

1. Appointments for participants requiring exempt infant formulas or WIC-eligible nutritionals in Food Package III must only be completed by a Competent Professional Authority (CPA). If a CPA is not in the clinic, other WIC staff must arrange for a CPA at a different site, the Local Agency (LA) Nutrition Education Coordinator, or State Agency (SA) nutritionist to complete the appointment. Document the consultation in the Management Information System (MIS). Refer to SA guidance for issuance of exempt infant formulas or WEN.

2. Obtain medical documentation before issuing exempt infant formula or WEN. Medical documentation must be submitted on the Pennsylvania WIC Formula Authorization Form (FAF) or may be accepted when submitted on healthcare professional letterhead or prescription form. Medical documentation must be complete regardless of the form it’s submitted in. Medical documentation is considered complete when it includes all of the following information:

PENNSYLVANIA DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH

Policy Number: 5.10 WIC State Agency USDA Approval Date: March 5, 2025 State Effective Date: May 5, 2025

POLICY MANUAL

5. NUTRITION AND BREASTFEEDING SERVICES.

5.10 Exempt Infant Formula and WIC-Eligible Nutritionals

Page 2 of 4

a. Name and Birth Date of the participant receiving formula(s) b. Name(s) and quantity(ies) of formula(s) being authorized for WIC issuance c. Medical condition and/or ICD-10 code that justifies need for the formula(s) being authorized d. Amount of formula(s) and length of use e. Any special instructions related to the preparation, and/or feeding frequency of the formula(s), if applicable f. Healthcare professional signature g. Medical office name and contact information h. Date medical documentation was completed/sent to WIC i. WIC foods restrictions and length of restriction (for infants 6 months of age and older, children, and women)

3. The amount of formula specified on the medical documentation must be used to determine the quantity of formula provided to the WIC participant. However, the amount provided cannot exceed the maximum monthly amount allowed by the Federal WIC Regulations. Refer to SA guidance on maximum monthly amounts allowed.

4. Medical documentation for exempt infant formula or WEN must be renewed every 6 months or more often based on the frequency listed on the medical documentation; with the exception of premature (pre-discharge) formulas and RTF formulas packaged in 2oz. bottles, which must be renewed on a monthly basis.

5. Participants eligible to receive exempt infant formula or WEN must have one or more medical conditions, as determined by a healthcare professional licensed to order patient diets under Pennsylvania State law.

a. Healthcare professionals who are licensed to order patient diets under Pennsylvania state law are Physicians, Certified Registered Nurse Practitioners (CRNP), Physician’s Assistants (PA), and Certified Nurse Midwives (CNM). Licensed Dietitian-Nutritionists (LDN) employed in the clinical setting may also authorize exempt infant formulas and WEN within their scope of practice. i. It is the responsibility of the signing LDN to ensure they remain within their scope of practice to authorize products for WIC participants.

b. Any participant presenting medical documentation requesting exempt infant formula or WEN solely for the purpose of enhancing nutrient intake or managing body weight without an underlying medical condition will not be able to receive exempt infant formula or WEN from WIC. Food Package III is not authorized for women, infants or children whose only condition is food allergy or intolerance which does not require the use of an exempt infant formula or WEN but can be managed with one of the other WIC food packages.

6. Exempt infant formulas or WEN may be provided to women, infants and children when medical documentation indicates that the participant has a medical condition that precludes or restricts the use of conventional foods or standard formulas. These products

PENNSYLVANIA DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH

Policy Number: 5.10 WIC State Agency USDA Approval Date: March 5, 2025 State Effective Date: May 5, 2025

POLICY MANUAL

5. NUTRITION AND BREASTFEEDING SERVICES.

5.10 Exempt Infant Formula and WIC-Eligible Nutritionals

Page 3 of 4 must be provided to participants in accordance with Food Package III for women, infants, and children with special dietary needs.

7. Formula may be provided for oral use or for administration via an enteral tube feeding (i.e. nasogastric tube, gastrostomy, or jejunostomy tube). Formulas administered parenterally (via peripheral or central venous catheter) are not allowed.

8. Formula must normally be provided as concentrated liquid or powder. Refer to Policy 5.08 Infant Formula, for issuing Ready-To-Feed formula.

9. Formulas may be issued individually or in combination with another formula according to the medical documentation received to best accommodate the participant's nutritional needs. However, the combined total quantity of these products issued monthly may not exceed the regulatory maximum monthly allowance.

a. To provide a combination of two or more formulas, refer to the medical documentation for amounts of each formula being requested, including the contract brand, if applicable. If amounts are not specified, contact the healthcare provider.

10. Medical documentation may be faxed or provided electronically to the LA or clinic. Verbal orders from the healthcare professional for exempt infant formulas and WEN can be accepted by a CPA on a case-by-case basis. Verbal orders must be clearly documented in the MIS including the date, name of healthcare professional providing verbal order, product and amount. Written confirmation of the medical documentation must be obtained within one month after the phone call and before providing additional benefits.

11. If a healthcare professional prescribes a formula which is not on the WIC-approved formula list, LA staff must contact the SA.

a. The medical documentation may be requested by the SA.

b. SA staff will review documentation of relevant assessment of formula preparation and infant feeding. If needed, SA may request a completed Bottle Feeding Checklist.

c. After reviewing the information, the SA may approve the formula for the specific participant by adding the product to the MIS, and LA WIC staff will be notified when the new product is available for ordering. It may take 24-48 hours before the LA staff will be able to order the formula through the warehouse or the participant may purchase at a WIC-authorized vendor-retailer store.

12. Refer to Policy 4.03, Special Formula Distribution Center, for information on ordering and delivering exempt infant formulas and WENs from the Special Formula Distribution Center (SFDC).

13. Exempt formulas and WEN must not be provided to participants while they are hospitalized, incarcerated, or institutionalized.

PENNSYLVANIA DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH

Policy Number: 5.10 WIC State Agency USDA Approval Date: March 5, 2025 State Effective Date: May 5, 2025

POLICY MANUAL

5. NUTRITION AND BREASTFEEDING SERVICES.

5.10 Exempt Infant Formula and WIC-Eligible Nutritionals

Page 4 of 4

14. PKU Formula Issuance:

a. When PKU formula is required, it will not be issued by WIC. PKU formula will be covered by the participant’s insurance or medical assistance. However, Food Package III and the PKU formula the participant is on must be selected when creating the participant’s food package in the MIS.

b. WIC will issue any non-PKU formula that is authorized. The total amount of all formula (non-PKU and PKU) must not exceed the USDA allowable maximum.

c. Medical Nutrition Therapy (MNT) is provided by a metabolic dietitian at a PKU Treatment Center. WIC nutrition education contacts are still required for appropriate topics such as, but not limited to, breastfeeding support, physical activity, and shopping on a budget.

d. In the case that the SA receives referral information, the SA nutritionist will contact the LA.

e. The LA will contact the patient referred to WIC for PKU formula to schedule a WIC appointment.

f. All endorsers and/or proxies of PKU participants must come to WIC at least tri- monthly for nutrition education contacts and issuance of allowed foods and/or standard infant formula. Endorsers must be seen by a CPA at each visit.

U.S. Department of Agriculture, Food and Nutrition Service, Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children (WIC), WIC Food Packages - Regulatory Requirements for WIC-Eligible Foods, https://www.fns.usda.gov/wic/wic-food-packages- regulatory-requirements-wic-eligible-foods#WIC-ELIGIBLE%20NUTRITIONAL (page last updated November 3, 2023)
